name: Crestview College
school_type: mixed boarding and day secondary school with a private-school identity and government-aligned regulation
structure: JSS1-JSS3 and SS1-SS3 with class streams, prefect hierarchy, house system, day/boarding split, and a strong academic discipline culture

reputation.academic: strong in mathematics, sciences, and commerce
reputation.extracurricular: solid but not elite; school pride matters and club culture is active
reputation.discipline: strict but uneven; students know which teachers and prefects are feared and which are mostly tolerated

history: Founded in the late 1990s by an educational trust seeking a disciplined, academically ambitious school for Abuja families. It grew rapidly and became known for exam performance, organised routines, and visible social hierarchy.
uniform: school tie or striped ties in upper classes
neat polished shoes and tidy presentation
discipline_culture: Students are expected to be punctual, respectful, and visibly obedient. Teachers and prefects enforce rules with a mix of formal authority and social pressure. The school is not perfectly fair, but it has a clear moral code that students learn quickly.
parent_relationship: Parents value grades, behaviour, and visible respectability. Good conduct matters almost as much as academic success, especially for families viewing Crestview as a middle-class route to stability and prestige.
community_relationship: The school sits in a residential and commercial area, so nearby shops, transport routes, and local religious communities are part of student life. The school has reputation and prestige, but also a strong image of being strict or elitist.

house_system.details: House competitions matter for sports and discipline points. House identity strengthens a student's visible school identity and creates real social rivalry without requiring a full sports management system.

boarding_day_support.boarding: Boarders have structured routines, stronger dorm culture, and heavier scrutiny. They are more tied to school life and its social rhythms.
boarding_day_support.day_students: Day students have more independence and more access to neighbourhood life, but less immersion in hostel culture and school routines.
